about.description: Indie Toolbox is a collection of everyday tools to help indie developers — and beyond — tackle their small daily tasks. No more hunting for software, installing apps, or relying on online services just to crop an image or mix some audio. I've gathered here, and will keep gathering, the tools I find missing in my own workflow. Best of luck with your products. May the Force and patience be with you, and return to you as the good fortune you deserve.

calendar.guideIntro: Setup for the GitHub Pages site. Menu and button names below match the English Google Cloud Console interface.
calendar.guideStep1Body: In Google Calendar on a computer, use Other calendars → Add other calendars (+) → Create new calendar. Name it, for example, Journey Book, then click Create calendar. This keeps project tasks separate from personal events.
calendar.guideStep2Body: Open Google Cloud Console. Select an existing project in the top bar, or create one via Select a project → New project. Complete all subsequent steps in the same project.
calendar.guideStep3Body: Go to APIs & Services → Library, find Google Calendar API, and click Enable. If you see Manage instead, the API is already enabled.
calendar.guideStep4Body: Go to Google Auth platform → Branding. If you see Get Started, enter an App name, select a User support email, provide Contact Information, and finish with Create. If it is already configured, continue.
calendar.guideStep5Title: Add your account to Test users
calendar.guideStep5Body: Go to Google Auth platform → Audience. For a personal Gmail account, choose External. While the app is in Testing, under Test users click Add users, enter the Google account you will connect, and click Save.
calendar.guideStep6Body: Go to Google Auth platform → Data Access → Add or Remove Scopes. Add both URIs below. If they are not listed, paste them under Manually add scopes, then click Add to Table → Update → Save.
calendar.guideStep7Body: Go to Google Auth platform → Clients → Create Client. Set Application type to Web application. Under Authorized JavaScript origins, click Add URI and enter the origin of the open site:
calendar.guideOriginNote: For the published Indie Toolbox site, use https://oxygenchick.github.io — without /Indie-Toolbox/ or /Tasks.html. If you also use a local preview, add its origin as a separate entry. Leave Authorized redirect URIs empty. Click Create and copy the Client ID ending in .apps.googleusercontent.com. No Client secret or API key is needed here.
calendar.guideStep8Body: Open or create the project JSON file. Click Google Calendar, paste the Client ID, and click Connect Google. Approve access, select the separate calendar, and click Use this calendar. Dated tasks become all-day events after the file saves.
calendar.guideNotesBody: origin_mismatch means the open site's address differs from Authorized JavaScript origins. Check the scheme, host, and port. If access is denied while in Testing, check Test users. Sync is one-way while the tab is open and Google access is active. When the token expires, click Connect Google again.
